faqs.question: Photo on CV?
faqs.answer: Common in Germany; keep it professional if used.

body:
Answer: An Ausbildung CV should be clear, honest and occupation-focused: contact details, education, German level, relevant skills/experience, and availability. Europass-style structure helps. Do not invent hospital hours or German levels.

Sections that matter

  1. Personal details + city/time zone
  2. Education with years
  3. Language levels (CEFR)
  4. Experience / volunteering related to the trade
  5. Skills and certificates

Common CV mistakes

  • Copying a Canadian résumé format with long paragraphs
  • Claiming B2 German with no certificate
  • Photo or design that breaks ATS readability

Build a draft in CV Builder then refine in consult.

Evidence standard before you spend

For anything related to ausbildung, germany, keep proofs that a third party can verify: offers on letterhead, bank PDFs with history, attestation receipts, and language results that match the program. Screenshots without context are not a file. If a seller asks you to hide a refusal, change the topic — that is not how SK Immigration works.

  • Offer/contract names match the passport spelling
  • Language rule is printed (IELTS score, MOI, German level, etc.)
  • Funds story matches 3–6 months of statements where missions care about history
  • Attestation order is destination-correct (Apostille vs MOFA paths are not toys)
  • Official mission or university pages were opened the same week you pay

Mistakes we see on “cv for ausbildung germany” files

  • Believing Ausbildung is available with zero German for nursing/tech roles
  • Paying cash to an unverifiable “German employer agent”
  • Submitting a degree-style SOP for a vocational contract
  • Ignoring recognition/language timelines until the flight week
